sources.entry: Prisme Analytics - Privacy-focused and progressive analytics service based on Grafana. (Source Code) AGPL-3.0/MIT Docker

summary.one_liner: Prisme Analytics is an open source, privacy-focused, cookie-less web analytics service built on Grafana dashboards that is designed to be self-hosted.
summary.what_it_does: Prisme provides a tracking script (about 2kB) that you add to a website to record pageviews and custom events. A noscript pixel endpoint supports tracking for visitors without JavaScript. The README says bots, scrapers and spam traffic are filtered out automatically, and that tracking is cookie-less and collects only anonymized data. Dashboards are built on Grafana, which supplies user, team, permission and multi-organization management plus custom dashboards. UTM parameters can be used to measure campaign and newsletter traffic. The README says the tracker works automatically with pushState-based frontend routers (SPA support). It also includes a k6 load-test setup with a published benchmark of over 50,000 requests per second on one machine.
use_cases: measuring marketing campaign and UTM traffic
custom event tracking for web apps
how_to_run: Follow the documentation guide to self-host a Prisme analytics instance (or use Prisme Cloud)
Add the Prisme tracking script (/static/wa.js, loaded with defer) to your website's HTML
Optionally add the noscript pixel tag pointing to /api/v1/noscript/events/pageviews for JavaScript-less tracking
Open the Web Analytics dashboard in Grafana to view data
notable: Cookie-less analytics with anonymized data, described as GDPR, PECR and Schrems II friendly
Tracking script around 2kB; no-JavaScript pixel fallback
Dashboards, users, teams and permissions inherited from Grafana
Automatic filtering of bots and spam traffic
Published k6 benchmark of over 50,000 req/s ingestion
caveats: Configuration details are only on the external website, not in the README
Performance figures are the author's own test on a single AMD Ryzen 7 machine with injectors on the same host
Licensing is AGPL-3.0-only with MIT exceptions described in LICENSING.md
